0.long_answer: The ATP-dependent ion transporter discovered in 1957 is the Na+/K+-ATPase, also known as the sodium-potassium pump. This enzyme, discovered by Jens Christian Skou in 1957, is crucial for maintaining the electrochemical gradients across the cell membrane by actively transporting sodium out of and potassium into the cell using ATP as an energy source. In the context provided, autoantibodies that impair alpha-enolase function can affect energy production within the cell, potentially compromising the activity of the Na+/K+-ATPase, thereby linking the autoimmune condition, encephalopathy, and thyroiditis with a disturbance in cellular ion balance.
